title: What I Actually Cook When I'm Too Tired to Cook
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Three dinners for nights when you have nothing left. Rough recipes below, measure with your heart.

1. Crispy chickpea rice bowl
2. Tomato egg drop thing
3. Peanut noodles that are mostly pantry

The pot in this video is fifteen years old and was my mum's.

Newsletter with the written recipes: priyacooks.substack.com

sentences.t: Hi, hello, welcome back, I look like this because it's been a very long week.
So today is a tired cooking video, which is my favorite kind of video, honestly.
No fancy stuff, no special trip to the shop, just what's already in my kitchen right now.
First one is a chickpea rice bowl, and the trick is you fry the chickpeas until they're actually crunchy.
Pat them dry first, like really dry, otherwise they spit at you and you will cry.
Little bit of oil, medium high, and then you just leave them alone, which is the hard part for me.
While those go, I'm doing leftover rice in the microwave with a splash of water and a plate on top.
Okay, so, while we wait, I have to tell you why I'm this tired, because it's actually kind of a funny story.
Last week I did my first ever commercial job, I got hired to develop recipes for Le Creuset's winter campaign.
They flew me to a studio in Manchester and I cooked the same braise eleven times in one day.
Eleven times, for the cameras, because every take the lid steamed up or the light changed.
And there was a person on set whose whole job was to make the onions look more golden with a paintbrush.
I didn't know that was a job, I have so much respect for her now.
Anyway, they paid me, I got to keep my apron, and I came home and slept for fourteen hours.
And no, this sad old pot is not one of theirs, this was my mum's and it has survived three house moves.
Okay, chickpeas, look at that, that's the sound you want, that little rattle.
Cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and a squeeze of lemon right at the end so the spices don't burn.
Rice in the bowl, chickpeas on top, a big spoon of yogurt, and whatever greens are about to die in your fridge.
Mine is half a bag of spinach, which I'm just wilting with the heat from the rice.
That's dinner one, and it took like fifteen minutes.
Second one is my tomato egg thing, which my partner calls the sad soup, but he eats two bowls every time.
Garlic and ginger in a little oil, then a tin of chopped tomatoes, and you cook it down until it's jammy.
Then water or stock, whatever you have, a spoon of soy, a pinch of sugar.
Now the egg part, beat two eggs and drizzle them in slowly while you stir in one direction.
See those ribbons?
That's it, that's the whole trick, if you dump them in all at once you get scrambled egg soup, which is also fine, honestly.
Spring onion on top, sesame oil, and I like a bit of chili crisp because I'm a menace.
Okay, last one, and this is the one I make most, peanut noodles from the back of the cupboard.
Any noodles, I'm using those cheap dried wheat ones, boil them a minute less than the packet says.
Sauce is peanut butter, soy, rice vinegar, a little honey, garlic, and hot noodle water to loosen it.
Whisk it in the bowl you're going to eat out of, because we are not making extra washing up tonight.
Noodles straight in, toss toss toss, and if you have a cucumber, slice it thin and pile it on.
I do not have a cucumber, I have a carrot, so we're shaving a carrot, it's going to be fine.
Mm, yeah, that's the one.
That's honestly what I ate three nights in a row after the shoot.
If you make any of these, tell me in the comments what you swapped, because I know nobody has all of this at once.
I didn't measure a single thing today, so the amounts I wrote down are honestly more like suggestions.
Okay, I'm going to eat this on the sofa and not move for the rest of the night.
Bye, love you, eat something warm.
